chapter: French Quarter music, then and now
title: Parties, passing the hat and tips
summary: Wood never attended student parties with bands and saw no collections at parades, only tips at the Paddock Lounge.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I was thinking about, we mentioned Irwin, did the students have any parties?
Well, if they did, I was a married graduate student, and I don't remember ever going to a party, You didn't go to a party with a band? Where there was live music, no, no.
Did people ever pass the hat, or ask for contributions anyway?

The only time, certainly not the brass bands, that played in the street, that I went to, never. I know the only extra contribution, that I remember being involved in, is when you made a request, at the paddock lounge, you'd throw them a couple of bucks,

and they would play a number for you, but I don't remember anybody. You weren't asked to buy a ticket, to any church function? No. I have seen, something I haven't seen in years, but, four people carrying a sheet, one in each corner. And ask people to throw money, and you throw money in it,
as they go by. I never saw, I don't remember seeing that, in any of the parades. Well then how do you know it?
Well I've seen it in other places, that they would,
at home, they'll do that. But I don't recall, ever seeing anybody, soliciting, your contribution, at one of those, occasions.
